verses.76:2: إِنَّا خَلَقۡنَا ٱلۡإِنسَٰنَ مِن نُّطۡفَةٍ أَمۡشَاجࣲ نَّبۡتَلِيهِ فَجَعَلۡنَٰهُ سَمِيعَۢا بَصِيرًا

meaning: The root مَشَجَ (mashaja) denotes mixing. Ibn Fāris gives its core simply as الخلط, citing نُطْفَة أَمْشَاج, a drop of mingled constituents; the singular مَشَج or مَشِيج names what has been blended together.
en_note: Manually curated for a Quranic hapax root.
meaning_previous: The root مَشِيجٌ (mashīj) refers to something mixed or confused, like two colors or substances blended.
meaning_source: Derived from the classical dictionaries (chiefly Maqayis al-Lugha, Ibn Faris d.1004) held in lexicon_full/
